subject: Economics
description: IMF, World Bank, WTO, ADB, BRICS, G20 — founding, HQ, function

questions.stem: The headquarters of the INTERNATIONAL MONETARY FUND (IMF) is in:

options.option_text: New York
Washington D.C.
Geneva
Paris

questions.explanation: IMF HQ: Washington D.C., USA. Founded 1944 at Bretton Woods Conference. 190 members (2023). Managing Director is traditionally European (currently Kristalina Georgieva). World Bank is also in Washington D.C. UN is in New York. WTO & WHO are in Geneva.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The WORLD TRADE ORGANIZATION (WTO) was established in the year:
questions.explanation: WTO founded 1 January 1995 out of the Uruguay Round (1986-94) of GATT negotiations, succeeding GATT (1947). HQ: Geneva. 164 members (2023). Ministerial Conference is the highest body.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: Match each ORGANISATION with its HEADQUARTERS. A. World Bank.  B. ADB.  C. OPEC.  D. WTO. List-II: 1. Washington D.C.  2. Manila.  3. Vienna.  4. Geneva.
questions.explanation: World Bank — Washington D.C. ADB (Asian Development Bank) — Manila, Philippines. OPEC (Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries) — Vienna, Austria. WTO — Geneva, Switzerland.

questions.stem: BRICS is a group of emerging economies. The founding members (as of the 2010 expansion to include South Africa) are:

options.option_text: Brazil, Russia, India, Canada, South Africa
Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa
Brazil, Russia, Indonesia, China, South Africa
Bangladesh, Russia, India, China, South Africa

questions.explanation: BRIC (Brazil, Russia, India, China) coined by Jim O'Neill (Goldman Sachs, 2001). South Africa added 2010 → BRICS. BRICS Summit 2023 (Johannesburg) admitted 6 more members (Egypt, Iran, UAE, Saudi Arabia, Ethiopia, Argentina — Argentina later withdrew) effective 2024.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The New Development Bank (NDB) — also called the 'BRICS Bank' — is headquartered in:

options.option_text: Beijing
Shanghai
Mumbai
Moscow

questions.explanation: NDB HQ: Shanghai, China. Established 2014 at the BRICS Fortaleza Summit; operational from 2015. First president: K. V. Kamath (India). Authorised capital: US$100 billion. Mandate: infrastructure + sustainable development in emerging economies.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) is headquartered in:

options.option_text: New Delhi
Kathmandu
Dhaka
Colombo

questions.explanation: SAARC HQ: Kathmandu, Nepal. Established 8 December 1985 (Dhaka Summit). 8 members: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka. SAARC summits have been suspended since 2014 due to India-Pakistan tensions; India now pushes BIMSTEC instead.

questions.stem: The G20 originated as a forum of Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors in 1999 and was elevated to a LEADERS' SUMMIT in:
questions.explanation: G20 Leaders' Summit began in November 2008 (Washington, during the financial crisis). Comprises 19 countries + the EU (soon to be the African Union too, admitted 2023). India hosted in 2023; Delhi Declaration. in response to the global financial crisis.

questions.stem: Which institution within the World Bank Group is specifically mandated to finance private-sector enterprises in developing countries without requiring a government guarantee?

options.option_text: IBRD — provides loans to middle-income governments
IFC — extends credit directly to private sector firms
IDA — offers concessional loans to the poorest nations
MIGA — guarantees investors against non-commercial risk

questions.explanation: IFC (International Finance Corporation), established in 1956, is the World Bank Group arm that lends to private businesses without requiring host-government guarantees — a key distinction. IBRD lends to creditworthy middle-income governments; IDA provides soft loans/grants to the poorest nations; MIGA offers political-risk insurance to investors, not direct loans.

questions.stem: The IMF's Special Drawing Rights (SDR) basket consisted of four currencies until 2016, when a fifth was added. Which currency was included in the SDR basket effective October 2016?

options.option_text: Indian Rupee (INR) — world's 5th largest economy
Chinese Renminbi (CNY) — added after 2015 IMF review
South Korean Won (KRW) — Asia's export powerhouse
Swiss Franc (CHF) — traditional global reserve asset

questions.explanation: In November 2015 the IMF approved adding the Chinese Renminbi (CNY) to the SDR basket, effective 1 October 2016, alongside the USD, EUR, GBP, and JPY. The INR has not yet met the 'freely usable' criterion; the KRW and CHF are not SDR basket currencies. The inclusion was recognition of China's growing role in global trade and finance.

questions.stem: India and Pakistan were admitted as full members of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) at which summit, and who hosted it?

options.option_text: 2015 Ufa Summit — Russia chaired the proceedings
2016 Tashkent Summit — Uzbekistan was chair nation
2017 Astana Summit — Kazakhstan hosted the ceremony
2018 Qingdao Summit — China hosted the proceedings

questions.explanation: At the June 2017 Astana Summit in Kazakhstan, India and Pakistan formally acceded as full SCO members, expanding membership from 6 to 8. The 2015 Ufa and 2016 Tashkent summits processed their memoranda of obligations as candidates. The 2018 Qingdao Summit (China) was India's first full-member summit participation — a common exam mix-up.

questions.stem: Unlike the IMF and World Bank where voting power is weighted by financial contribution, the WTO primarily makes decisions through which mechanism?

options.option_text: Weighted voting proportional to GDP contribution
Consensus-based, with each member holding one vote
Executive Board decides by simple majority vote
Rotating presidency among developed-nation blocs

questions.explanation: WTO decisions are taken by consensus as the default method; when voting does occur, each member holds one equal vote regardless of trade volume or GDP — making it fundamentally different from the IMF (quota-weighted) and World Bank (share-weighted). Option A describes IMF/WB. Option C is incorrect — WTO has no Executive Board with majority-vote power. Option D has no basis in WTO governance.

questions.stem: The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) places jurisdictions on its 'grey list' when they commit to addressing deficiencies in combating which specific threats?

options.option_text: Tax evasion and illicit capital flight from borders
Money laundering and financing of terrorism or WMDs
Corruption and bribery in public procurement systems
Cybercrime and digital-asset exchange manipulation

questions.explanation: FATF was established in 1989 (G7 Paris Summit) to set international standards for combating money laundering (AML) and financing of terrorism and WMD proliferation (CFT/CPF). The 'grey list' (Jurisdictions Under Increased Monitoring) flags countries with strategic AML/CFT gaps. Tax evasion is primarily the OECD's domain; corruption/bribery falls under UNCAC and the World Bank, not FATF.

questions.stem: When the IMF's 14th General Review of Quotas was finally implemented in January 2016, which country moved into the top three quota-holders for the first time, displacing an existing developed-economy member?

options.option_text: India — elevated on the strength of its GDP growth
Brazil — representing South America's largest share
China — rose from 6th to 3rd largest quota holder
Russia — gained weight as a BRICS anchor economy

questions.explanation: The 14th Review doubled overall quotas and shifted ~6% of quota shares toward dynamic emerging economies. China's share rose to ~6.4%, moving it from 6th to 3rd place (behind only the USA and Japan), overtaking Germany, France, and the UK. India moved from 11th to 8th. Brazil and Russia also gained shares but did not enter the top three — a specific recall point examiners have tested.

questions.stem: Under the WTO Agreement on Safeguards, a member country may impose temporary import restrictions without proving unfair trade practices. Which precise condition must be demonstrated to lawfully invoke safeguard measures?

options.option_text: Dumping — imports priced below their normal value
Serious injury caused by an unforeseen import surge
Foreign government subsidy distorting trade flows
Persistent trade deficit exceeding 5% of GDP target

questions.explanation: Under Article XIX GATT / WTO Agreement on Safeguards, three cumulative conditions must be met: (i) imports have increased absolutely or relatively, (ii) the domestic industry suffers serious injury or threat thereof, and (iii) the surge resulted from 'unforeseen developments.' No proof of unfair practice is required — that is the critical distinction: dumping triggers anti-dumping duties (Option A, AD Agreement); subsidies trigger countervailing duties (Option C, SCM Agreement). Option D has no basis in WTO law.
